placements.why: The envelope's entire content is an observatory calibration record (note title: 'Observatory Calibration: Kestrelwood Spectrograph'). No existing strata category exists in this repo to hold it (structure is empty), and 'Calibration' is named among the org's recognized top-level strata categories per the role description. Nothing existing is close enough to warrant an INSPIRED lineage edge — this is a foundational NEW mint with no required parent.
placements.title: Observatory Instrument Calibration as an Organizational Category
placements.theme: Calibration work — bringing an instrument to a verified, trusted operating state — is tracked as its own organizational concern distinct from Product, Architecture, or Proof.

placements.title: Instrument Readiness Established Through Reference-Verified Calibration
placements.theme: An observatory instrument's calibration is trusted only once it is checked against an established reference standard and confirmed to hold across its full operating range.
placements.why: src-1 states the calibration value; src-2 supplies the verification act (checked against June reference plates, holding across the full observing band) that grounds trust in that value; src-3 is the session's declarative record consolidating both into one instrument/calibration entry. Per the grain test, the specific 88.4 MHz figure and the June-plates check are one-time facts/measurements — they are evidence, not a leaf themselves — but together they evidence a recurring thematic subject (verifying instrument calibration against reference data before it is trusted) that future calibration envelopes for other instruments would keep feeding. No existing narrative leaf exists in this empty repo to hold this theme, so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
